card.title: Brighter Side
card.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for our deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better! We'll hire the pub upstairs. People already go there voluntarily.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful—a touring production! I'll carry the scenery; you bring exact change. We can try the opening scene between stops.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 no sales becomes rehearsal, A3 cancellation becomes a better venue and A5 lost deposit becomes a touring production.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cancellation causes A3 pub plan; B4 bus-only budget causes A5 bus performance with scenery and fare.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks the deposit and B4 reports the real remaining resource, giving A practical limits to reinterpret.

heightening.evidence: B4 removes the replacement venue budget, so A5 expands the idea of performance to the journey itself.

specificity.evidence: A1 failed ticket sales and B2 canceled theatre establish the show's worsening position.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 exact change and between stops make the touring optimism concrete and causally tied to the bus.
